proposal:
SCOPE. Hand-derived, nothing executed. One unimplemented root rule, FAP-D (flip-automorphism pivoting with a defect ladder). It widens a tractable family with polynomial discovery and certificate cost. It is not a SAT algorithm and bounds no ELIM trace. My 00043 peak prediction failed (4 predicted, 2 observed), so I predict no deployed peak; fixture is null.

MECHANISM. flip_t negates the variables in t. It sends a clause with support S and forbidden point q to support S, point q+t|S, so it preserves the clause set iff P_B+t|S=P_B for every exact-support block B.
1. K0=∩_B(Stab(P_B)⊕F2^([n]∖S_B)) is therefore exactly the flip-automorphism group. Cost is O(L²+Ln²) bit operations for encoding length L: m_B candidate differences per block, then one kernel. No caps, no 2^n table.
2. Take a reduced echelon basis of K, choosing pivots greedily by number of core blocks containing the variable, then smaller ID. Add units ¬x_π. No quotient CNF, right inverse or compatible basis is needed: a model of the restricted formula is a model of F. BLQ stays first where its basis is compatible (narrower clauses); FAP replaces the incompatible_greedy_basis skip.
3. Ladder for punctured blocks. Let r_B(t)=|P_B∩(P_B+t)| over pair differences. For δ=0..max m_B: T_B^δ={t: m_B−r_B(t)≤δ}; H_B is the largest T_B^δ', δ'≤δ, that is a subspace; K^δ is the intersection of the extensions. Core G = clauses whose whole K^δ-orbit lies in F; E=F∖G; Ĝ=G plus pivot units.
4. Answers. (i) Any refutation of Ĝ gives UNSAT, since G⊆F. The polynomial variant runs only Canon/SCC/2SAT/capped IALH on Ĝ; handing Ĝ to ELIM inherits unbounded cost. (ii) If Σ_{C∈E}2^(−ρ(C))<1, with ρ(C)=dim K|supp(C), then F is satisfiable iff Ĝ is (T36). (iii) Otherwise UNKNOWN; solver and order untouched.
Certificate: K basis, pivots, core list. The checker tests closure of the core under each basis flip by set lookup, O(L·dim K), independent of discovery and of n.

INDEPENDENT-TEST PREDICTIONS (hand-computed; any mismatch falsifies).
P1. 00043 fixture (deployed: skip, peak 2). K0=span{{1,3,5,7,9},{2,4,6,8,10}}, pivots 1,2. Ĝ has 28 clauses on variables 3..10: [3,4],[5,6],[7,8],[9,10] plus the 24 clauses avoiding variables 1,2.
P2. Neon 00049 (deployed: skip no_dimension_reduction, peak 16). With a=x1+x2+x3, b=x4+x5+x6, c=x7+x8+x9, d=x10+x11+x12, the six 16-clause blocks are (a∨b)(c∨d)(¬a∨¬c)(¬b∨¬d)(¬b∨¬c)(¬a∨¬d). K0=0. On coordinates (1,5,6,8,9,11,12) the 8-clause block has T^2=H=span{{9,12},{6,12},{1,5,6,8,9,11,12}}: it is the coset 0000101+H with point 0000000 moved to 0110000. For δ=2..7, dim K=4. At δ=8 both width-7 blocks are unconstrained, dim K=8, pivots are 1,2,4,5,7,8,10,11, E is the ten width-7 clauses, and Ĝ={[3,6],[9,12],[-3,-9],[-6,-12],[-6,-9],[-3,-12]}, refuted by 2SAT. On this reading the deployed peak 16 is a compression failure, not intrinsic hardness.
P3. 00043 fixture plus, per vertex pair i<j, the clause (u_i∨v_i∨u_j∨¬v_j). Every block has 5 points, so deployed compression should skip. The ladder at δ=1 returns P1's K and Ĝ with |E|=10 and Σ=10/4, so only (i) applies; Ĝ still needs a real refutation.
P4. P1's blocks restricted to the 5-cycle 12,23,34,45,15, plus any three new clauses on edge supports: Σ=3/4, so satisfiable, and some K-translate of every model of G satisfies E.
missing_theorem:
Hand-proved, unformalized (Lean targets):
T35. If flip_t preserves the clause set then F(x+t)=F(x); with echelon pivots, F is satisfiable iff F plus the pivot units is. K0 is the full flip-automorphism group. This is a general statement needing no enumeration.
T36. For C∈E the bad translates {k∈K:(x+k)|S=q} are empty or a coset of a subgroup of index 2^ρ(C). If Σ2^(−ρ)<1, every model of G has a K-translate satisfying E, found by conditional expectations over a basis of K. Tight: all 2^k sign patterns on k variables with K=F2^k give Σ=1 and UNSAT. Beyond the bound the fibre question is SAT itself (take G empty, K everything), so no polynomial rule decides it in general unless P=NP.
T37. If P=A⊔D, H=Stab(A), |D|≤δ and |H|>δ+|D|, then T^δ=H. Proof: t∈H loses at most |D| points; t∉H makes A∩(A+t) miss a whole H-coset, so the defect is at least |H|−|D|. It covers added points only, not deleted or moved ones (P2's block decodes anyway, outside the theorem).

FIRST MISSING THEOREM T40 (gap-free core discovery). Promise: F⊇G, G invariant under some subspace K, Ĝ an unsatisfiable 2-CNF. Find such (K,G), or any refutation, in time polynomial in L. The ladder does this only under T37's gap in every block of G. Without the gap I have neither an algorithm nor a hardness proof. Conjecture: NP-hard, because a block can carry two equal-defect decodings and a consistent global choice looks like a constraint problem.
Second gap T41: no inequality relates the deployed ELIM peak on Ĝ to that on F; the heuristic acceptance rule need not be monotone under unit restriction.
self_attack:
1. Flip (phase-shift) symmetries and breaking them by units are probably folklore in symmetry-breaking work; not checked against the literature. The new content is the exactness and cost statement, the ladder, T36 and T37.
2. Encoding adversary: split every wide clause with a private auxiliary, (a∨b∨z)(¬z∨c∨d). A flip must then permute the auxiliaries, so K0=0 and the ladder finds nothing. The 36-clause case becomes 72 clauses on 48 variables. Repair needs signed-permutation automorphisms, a graph-isomorphism-type discovery I do not propose.
3. Dense decoys: T37 fails once |D|≥|H|/2. For the 36-clause case (|H|=4) one extra point per block is recovered; two are not guaranteed. T^δ can stop being a subspace, and the block then falls back to {0}, killing K.
4. T36 is weak: the 36+9 control has Σ=9/4, and T36's hardness half says this cannot be fixed in general.
5. No trace guarantee. P1's Ĝ is 4-colouring of K5 with one vertex fixed and probably still needs ELIM. A 2-dimensional K does not make colouring tractable.
6. P2's fresh-support blocks would also be dropped by 00043's FNL; only the in-block decoding is new there. For δ=2..7 the intermediate Ĝ is wider and may defeat the polynomial pass. The r_B counts were done by hand.
7. K0 is syntactic. The translation stabilizer of the model set can be larger, and I make no claim about computing it.
mechanism_signature: FAP-D | unimplemented | root-only | K0 = exact flip-automorphism group, O(L²+Ln²), uncapped | pivot units instead of quotient CNF; no basis compatibility, no right inverse | certificate = K basis + pivots + core list, checked syntactically in O(L·dim K) | defect ladder δ=0..max block size, threshold sets must be subspaces | UNSAT via core G⊆F; SAT via Σ2^(−ρ)<1 or an evaluated model | UNKNOWN leaves solver and order intact | no claim on private-auxiliary encodings, signed permutations, dense decoys, auto00008, or deployed ELIM work
delta_from_prior: 00042's SQ left the choice of K as an unbounded search; 00043's FNL avoided K but had no answer to points added inside blocks. New: (1) at δ=0, K is not a search but an exactly computed group with a polynomial bound; (2) pivot units remove the quotient CNF, the right inverse, the compatible basis and the 2^n certificate; (3) the defect ladder with T37 recovers stabilizers under in-block extra points; (4) T36 gives SAT-side lifting with tightness and a hardness boundary; (5) hand decoding of 00049, including its perturbed coset. Dropped: FNL's r^ν branching, and any deployed peak prediction after the 00043 failure.
